scope: Adversarial review of the decision-grade plan and its explicitly non-shipping prototype contracts, focused on GitHub/App/webhook trust, prompt injection, credentials, sandboxing, supply chain, SQL roles, approvals, tenancy, effect replay, audit, and self-modification. Prototype gaps are expressed as implementation and admission gates, not as claims that the prototype ships.
strengths: The threat model correctly treats issues, repository content, logs, tool output, and model output as untrusted data and keeps authorization in deterministic gateways.
The plan separates proposal, approval, execution, verification, merge, deployment, and promotion identities and calls for exact-digest approvals and current lease fences.
GitHub guidance covers raw-body HMAC validation, durable deduplication, authoritative rereads, minimum App permissions, full-SHA Actions, fork isolation, and merge_group checks.
Operations explicitly stop blind retries for unknown effects, revoke capabilities before cleanup, and require isolated author/verifier environments.
Documents clearly label the controller and production controls as proposed, which avoids overstating prototype maturity.

findings.title: Prototype SQL has no repository or installation tenant boundary
findings.requirement: The multi-repository plan requires an immutable tenant key on every row and database-enforced cross-repository isolation.
findings.reproduction: Apply migrations, insert work_items for repos A and B, then SET ROLE polar_runtime; SELECT * FROM polar.work_items; both are visible and either row is updateable. polar_auditor can likewise read every webhook payload. No table enables RLS.
findings.impact: A credential scoped operationally to one repository can read or mutate another repository, and global keys/queues can collide across tenants. This blocks any multi-tenant deployment, although the prototype is explicitly non-shipping.
findings.recommendation: Add an immutable installation/tenant FK to every record, namespace inbox/idempotency/effect keys by it, use FORCE RLS or tenant-specific connection roles, and make cross-tenant denial a production-admission gate.
findings.verification: Negative SQL tests under every role must prove cross-tenant SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and cross-tenant FK substitution fail, including prepared statements and owner-bypass cases.

findings.title: Approval records are self-asserted rather than authenticated and purpose-bound
findings.requirement: Every consequential approval must prove a verified human principal, authorized role/quorum, independence, exact action/content scope, and expiry.
findings.reproduction: Construct ApprovalEnvelope(approved_by='attacker-claims-human', approver_kind='human', expires_at=None) over an attacker-computed digest and call create_run_context; it succeeds. In SQL, a rejected, expired MERGE approval with a matching hash can back a READY decision; deployments/eval promotions accept an unrelated approval_id.
findings.impact: An agent or compromised service can manufacture apparent human authorization, reuse the wrong approval purpose, or create a never-expiring approval.
findings.recommendation: Require cryptographically/authenticated principal provenance, role snapshot, source review ID, quorum set, purpose/action scope, finite expiry, and purpose-dependent candidate/artifact/environment fields. Make approval creation append-only through a narrow gate and bind all fields into the digest.
findings.verification: Add negative Python/schema/SQL tests for forged kind, absent expiry, self-approval, wrong role/quorum/purpose/item/SHA/environment, rejected/expired/invalidated records, and approval replay.

findings.title: The fail-closed validator accepts capability and factory privilege expansion
findings.requirement: Mandatory denies, maximum capabilities, tools, secrets, network, budgets, and composition must be typed and non-overridable.
findings.reproduction: In a temp copy set implementer network.default=allow, secrets=[production], github_permissions={administration: write}, or add unrestricted_shell to factory tools. python .agent-os/bin/validate.py still prints 'validation passed'.
findings.impact: A protected-config mistake or malicious PR can be validator-green while granting exactly the powers the plan says factories cannot acquire.
findings.recommendation: Create strict schemas and semantic allowlists for capabilities, factories, registry, and composition. Enforce inherited mandatory denies, capability intersections, known tool/secret/egress classes, safe registry paths, and non-weakenable gates.
findings.verification: Maintain malicious fixtures for each escalation dimension and require every fixture to fail validation.

findings.title: Workflow validation misses .yaml files and does not enforce Actions security policy
findings.requirement: All workflows must receive semantic checks for least privilege, immutable actions, untrusted triggers, secret separation, and unsafe interpolation.
findings.reproduction: Add .github/workflows/evil.yaml containing invalid YAML; the validator exits 0 because it scans only **/*.yml. A valid .yml using an unpinned action or privileged pull_request_target is merely parsed and also passes.
findings.impact: An unsafe workflow can pass the named desired-config gate and expose tokens or run fork-controlled code in a privileged context.
findings.recommendation: Scan both extensions and add actionlint/zizmor plus policy checks for top/job permissions, full-SHA uses, dangerous event/checkout combinations, secrets, environments, caches, and expression-to-shell flows.
findings.verification: Run the gate against fixtures for .yaml syntax failure, mutable action refs, write-all permissions, privileged pull_request_target checkout, unsafe shell interpolation, and fork secret exposure.

findings.title: Untrusted planning output is represented as executable command strings
findings.requirement: Issue/repository/model prose must never become executable authority; commands must be protected IDs with typed arguments resolved outside the model.
findings.reproduction: Place shell metacharacters or a second command in a ticket verification_commands value or REPOSITORY_TEST_COMMAND. The published schemas/validator accept the string and define no command catalog or argv boundary.
findings.impact: If a future controller shells these documented fields, issue/repository prompt injection becomes command execution and can cross the worker boundary.
findings.recommendation: Define a plan schema that carries command IDs and typed argv only. Resolve IDs against a protected, digest-pinned catalog in the capability proxy; forbid shell evaluation and bind resolved argv/catalog digest to approval.
findings.verification: Adversarial tests must show command substitution, metacharacters, newlines, environment expansion, path escapes, and injected command IDs are rejected before sandbox execution.

findings.title: Effect records allow blind UNKNOWN replay and mutable intent/receipt substitution
findings.requirement: Unknown outcomes must stop retry; effect intent must be immutable and attempts/receipts must remain bound to one effect.
findings.reproduction: As polar_reconciler UPDATE an UNKNOWN outbox row back to PENDING or change its payload/hash/key; both are granted. Insert two unfinished effect_attempts. Create E1/E2, attempt A for E1, then a receipt with effect_id=E2 and attempt_id=A; the independent FKs accept it.
findings.impact: A reconciler bug or compromise can replay an ambiguous external action, rewrite the approved intent, or forge evidence that the wrong effect succeeded.
findings.recommendation: Make intent fields immutable; expose CAS transition procedures; allow UNKNOWN to leave only with a bound observation/receipt or reviewed decision; allow one unfinished attempt; add composite (attempt_id,effect_id) receipt binding.
findings.verification: Concurrency and crash tests must prove UNKNOWN cannot be queued blindly, only one active attempt exists, payload/key cannot change, and cross-effect receipts fail.

findings.title: Database grants collapse controller, lifecycle, approval, deploy, promotion, and audit authority
findings.requirement: A compromised component or one service credential must not manufacture the entire authorization and delivery history.
findings.reproduction: SET ROLE polar_runtime, then INSERT an approval, UPDATE work_items.lifecycle_state directly to DONE, INSERT a deployment/promoted candidate, and INSERT an audit row claiming another actor. The blanket all-table DML grant permits these operations; lifecycle has only an enum check.
findings.impact: One runtime credential bypasses separation of duties and can forge both the protected action and its apparent audit trail. polar_reconciler can also append canonical event_ledger rows despite the controller-only invariant.
findings.recommendation: Split ingress, controller, dispatcher, reconciler, merger, deployer, promoter, and audit-writer roles. Revoke raw DML on authority tables and expose narrow checked procedures deriving actor identity from authenticated session context. Anchor audit externally.
findings.verification: A full SET ROLE matrix must prove every identity can perform only its intended transitions and cannot forge actor, approval, lifecycle, deployment, promotion, or audit facts.

findings.title: Cross-work-item foreign keys permit authorization and evidence substitution
findings.requirement: Specs, attempts, approvals, deployments, outcomes, observations, and receipts must be bound to the same tenant and work item.
findings.reproduction: Create W1/W2 and spec S2 owned by W2, then UPDATE work_items SET current_spec_revision_id=S2 WHERE id=W1 and COMMIT; it succeeds. Similar bare-ID relationships accept another item's attempt, approval, deployment, or observation.
findings.impact: A valid high-trust artifact or approval from one work item can be substituted into another, becoming cross-tenant privilege escalation once multi-repository operation is enabled.
findings.recommendation: Carry tenant/work_item in each dependent key and use composite foreign keys consistently; keep semantic purpose/digest checks in locked gate procedures.
findings.verification: Add one negative mismatch test per relationship and randomized integrity tests across multiple tenants/items.

findings.title: The context contract permits unsigned, non-worker-bound bundles
findings.requirement: Workers must verify a signed, expiring context bound to issuer, audience, attempt, fence, cancellation epoch, and exact capability scope.
findings.reproduction: Call create_run_context without signing_key; it returns signature_scheme='none'. The repository context schema has no signature/key ID, worker identity, issuer/audience, path/command/egress/secret scope, or cancellation epoch and forbids additional fields.
findings.impact: A future runner following the current contract cannot distinguish an authentic scoped controller bundle from an unsigned/replayed one without an undocumented external mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Make signed envelopes mandatory at execution admission, define verification/key rotation/replay behavior, and bind all authority fields including worker audience, expiry, attempt/fence, cancellation epoch, and capabilities.
findings.verification: Round-trip sign/verify tests must reject unsigned, wrong audience/key, expired, revoked-epoch, altered capability, and stale-fence bundles.

findings.title: Validator bootstrap is version-pinned but not integrity-pinned
findings.requirement: The policy gate supply chain must use fully resolved, hash-verified dependencies and a digest-pinned execution image.
findings.reproduction: Inspect .agent-os/requirements.txt: it pins two direct versions but supplies no --hash entries or transitive lock; the workflow installs from the default index without --require-hashes.
findings.impact: Index, package, or transitive compromise can execute during installation or corrupt the validator that protects policy.
findings.recommendation: Generate a fully resolved hash lock, install with --require-hashes from an approved mirror, pin the runner/container toolchain digest where possible, and record it in evidence.
findings.verification: CI must fail for a changed wheel hash, unlisted transitive dependency, non-approved index, or mutable validator image.

findings.title: Role migration preserves dangerous pre-existing role attributes and grants
findings.requirement: Role installation must fail closed when named roles already have LOGIN, privilege attributes, memberships, or stale direct grants.
findings.reproduction: Before migration CREATE ROLE polar_agent LOGIN; then run migrations. The conditional CREATE leaves LOGIN and memberships/attributes intact, while security migration revokes PUBLIC only and the test checks only schema usage and one table privilege.
findings.impact: A reused or pre-provisioned role name can retain login, BYPASSRLS, inherited membership, or stale grants despite comments and tests claiming an isolated marker role.
findings.recommendation: Assert and normalize NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, NOCREATEROLE, NOCREATEDB, NOLOGIN, memberships, ownership, direct/default privileges, or abort installation on mismatch.
findings.verification: Seed hostile pre-existing roles and grants, run migrations, and verify the full attributes/membership/object/default-privilege matrix.

residual_uncertainty: No webhook ingress, GitHub App broker, capability proxy, sandbox launcher, merger, or deployer exists here for dynamic attack; those controls remain unverified until implementation.
SQL reproductions require PostgreSQL with migrations applied. Static grants and constraints make the described paths deterministic, but DATABASE_URL was unavailable in this review environment.
External GitHub rulesets, required CODEOWNER enforcement, App installation permissions, environment protection, and secret-store policy were not observable.
Python unit tests passed. The desired-config validator passed with its dependencies, but neither result exercises a production control plane.
